original.target_description: Unassigned side; placeholder only, not reassessed.

replication.target_description: Replication of Study 6: indirect effect of randomized high/low organisational hierarchy through perceived corruption on willingness to sign the petition. Matched by named mediator and outcome in Hypothesis 2, not row order or numeric correspondence.

n.sample_role: Participants in the final mutually exclusive high- and low-hierarchy groups contributing to the Study 6 mediation analysis.
n.exclusions: Incomplete study responses and participants requesting that their data not be used were excluded. The report states that data from all other full completers were analysed; exclusion counts are not specified.
n.location: Methodology, Design and Sample; Results, Study 6, Tables 1 and 2 (hierarchy-group Ns and both trust outcomes)
n.quote: Participants who did not complete all aspects of the study were automatically excluded from the analysis. ... participants were excluded if they responded “No – do not use my data” ... Data was analysed from all other participants who completed the study in full. ... High Hierarchy (N = 168) ... Low Hierarchy (N = 153)

p.location: Results, Study 6, Hypothesis 2 (indirect effects via perceived corruption)
p.quote: with a significant indirect effect (B = -.03, SE = 0.05, 95% CI [-0.06, -0.01])

notes: Identity checked independently from document content: title matches Corruption and Hierarchy: A Replication of Studies 1c and 6 of Fath & Kay 2018; named authors Thomas Rhys Evans, Renata Kviatkovskyte, Susannah O’Regan, Shernay A Adolph, Nishat Tasnim, Floriana O Nkagbu Chukwudi, Tereza Wildova and Maja M Krzan correspond to the supplied reference (which abbreviates/mangles some names). Document states Accepted for Publication at the Journal of General Psychology and includes methods, results, discussion, references and contributorship; it is a primary replication manuscript, not merely an abstract or preregistration. Project identity https://osf.io/zb5j2 is printed. The assigned DOI 10.31234/osf.io/68jft and reference year 2024 are not independently printed in this text, so precise DOI/version linkage remains unconfirmed. No PDF was supplied; section/table locators are used because this canonical text has no page markers. Only assigned unfinished fields n_r and pval_value_r were assessed. Final analytic N is documented by mutually exclusive randomized Study 6 groups, both outcomes tabulated in Table 2, and the explicit complete-case analysis policy: 168 + 153 = 321 participants. This is not derived from degrees of freedom or the recruitment total. No extra mediation-only exclusions are reported. Exclusion counts are unknown. The indirect effect for willingness to sign the petition is reported with B, SE and 95% CI but without a p-value; the p-values printed for hierarchy-to-corruption and corruption-to-outcome paths belong to different tests and are not substituted. Unassigned original, effect-size and reported-success fields are placeholders only. Printed indirect-effect evidence: with a significant indirect effect (B = -.03, SE = 0.05, 95% CI [-0.06, -0.01]).
